citation: McEwen, A. S. and Soderblom, L. A. 1983, Two classes of volcanic plumes on Io, Icarus 55, 191 doi:10.1016/0019-1035(83)90075-1
note: Prometheus-type plumes are long-lived and erupt at about 0.5 km/s; Pele-type plumes are short-lived and erupt at about 1.0 km/s; Abstract gives both vent speeds exactly as claimed. Volume and page are confirmed by [Geissler et al. 2003](https://consensus.app/papers/details/w:c558e4a9-72ec-4dc5-9f63-08f53f9b3f5e/?utm_source=claude_desktop), which cites Icarus 55 (1983) 191.

claims: format!("A {h:.0} km ballistic plume: gas leaves the vent at {speed:.0} m/s into almost no air, height v²/2g (McEwen and Soderblom 1983 speeds).")

Thin or no air: plume height v^2/(2g); vent speeds about 0.5 km/s for long-lived Prometheus-type plumes and about 1.0 km/s for short Pele-type eruptions on Io (McEwen and Soderblom 1983). Heights follow from the formula, not from the paper
